implementation_notes: dict is the document - arbitrary string keys, arbitrary values, nesting - so no Document/AbstractDocument pair is written at all; the interesting half is the view, which has three standard forms: TypedDict when a dict payload should be checked statically (zero runtime cost, enforced only by the type checker), dataclasses for objects the program constructs itself, and pydantic BaseModel when the document crosses a system boundary and needs runtime validation via model_validate. Attribute-style views over the same dict are a __getattr__ or a property away, and functools.cached_property keeps reads cheap. Type safety is layered per boundary rather than bought by a hand-written struct hierarchy. msgspec.Struct is the fast alternative to pydantic: field types are validated at decode time (msgspec.json.decode(..., type=Car)), it raises msgspec.ValidationError on mismatch, and it generates JSON Schema automatically via msgspec.json.schema(Car). Use it when throughput matters or when a validation-error-first boundary layer is preferred.
code_sketch:
class CarView(TypedDict):          # static view over a dict payload
    model: str
    price: int

doc: dict[str, object] = json.loads(payload)
view = cast(CarView, doc)          # checker-enforced view["model"], view["price"]
car = CarModel.model_validate(doc) # runtime-validated view at a boundary
pitfalls: TypedDict is erased at runtime and is not a dict subclass: isinstance fails against it and a wrong value type is caught only by the checker.
json.loads yields dict[str, Any], so every accessor without validation is an unchecked cast in disguise and a renamed key surfaces as a KeyError deep in the call chain.
Dataclasses and pydantic models copy data out of the document, so writes through the view no longer reach the original dict (unlike views over one shared map).
